evidence_quotes.section1_open: Rep skips quid pro quo entirely. Asks for date, name, email, phone number but never frames the 10–15 minute time box or promise of a dependable quote. Immediately moves into 'I'm just gonna ask you a quick questions' without a clear 'does that sound good to you?' gate.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked only after extensive logistics probing: 'Alright we'll, okay. So let me discuss with you the pricing and the estimate here but before that's awesome, do you have any other concerns aside from the price?' — probing on square footage, stories, pod dimensions, appliances, valuables, and boxes all happened first.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — customer raised only one concern (price curiosity: 'No, just curious about what this would cost'), and it required no follow-up depth.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no multiple concerns raised, so no reflection needed or attempted.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details: Partial. Gathered: property type (house), stories (2), square footage (1,529), pod dimensions and count (4 pods, 8'x5', 257 cu ft each), heavy items (couch, love seat, vanity), large appliances (70-inch TV). Missing: number of rooms, walking distance to property, additional rooms beyond main floor/upstairs, special considerations beyond what was volunteered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services: Not offered. Rep never asked if customer wants packing into boxes.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Asked, but customer couldn't estimate: 'Do you have an estimated number of boxes?' / 'Boxes, how many boxes do you think I have no idea?' Rep accepted and moved on, no typical-box-count anchor or overflow check offered.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Partial. Rep gives hourly rate ($111/mover, $222 for two movers) and minimum ($555 for 2.5 hours) but does not anchor to a typical range for this home size or personalize based on customer's stated move scope. No reference to how long similar unload jobs take.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full. Rep clearly states: hourly rate, what's included (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wraps, pads, tools), what's excluded (no heat fees, no credit card fees, no territory fees, no disassemble/reassemble fee, no transportation fee, no hidden fees of any type), and minimum (2.5 hours, prorated in 15-minute increments after).
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_silence: Not asked. After quoting $555, customer immediately pivots: 'can you email me the quote over' — rep never asks 'Does that feel fair?' and never pauses to let customer absorb or respond.
evidence_quotes.closes_loop: False. Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or any version of it.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Rep moves directly from pricing ($555) to email send-off: 'Yeah, of course I'll send this to your email and then if ever you're ready to book with us just reply to that email, or give us a call.'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked. No 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' type question.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked. Rep never says 'Would you like our help with your move?' or any variant. Customer initiates the close request ('can you email me the quote') and rep accommodates: 'Yeah, of course I'll send this to your email... just reply to that email, or give us a call.'
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: None. No date, phone, arrival window, crew size, addresses, or crew notes confirmed. Rep only commits to emailing the quote and tells customer to reply or call back.

top_strength: Jeline gathered detailed logistics information efficiently — pod dimensions, item weights, appliance specs, and special items — building a solid picture of the actual unload scope.
coaching_note: Jeline never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' and allowed the customer to drive the close instead of leading with an explicit ask; she also skipped Section 1's time-box framing, the Two Promises entirely, and any final concerns check, cutting the call short by roughly half the script.
